chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

Four men testified against a man who was muhsan (married/free) for adultery, then one of them returned [to the court] after the man was killed. He said: 'If the one who returned said, "I made a mistake," the hadd punishment is inflicted and diya (blood money) is paid. And if he said, "I did it deliberately," he is killed.'

key_terms.أَوْهَمْتُ: I made a mistake or erred
key_terms.الْحَدَّ: The fixed punishment prescribed by Sharia
key_terms.مُحْصَن: A free, married Muslim man, subject to stricter adultery penalties

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one of four witnesses against a muhsan retracts his testimony after execution?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *kaffarat al-shahada* (expiation of testimony) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between unintentional error (*wahm*) and deliberate falsehood (*ta'ammud*) regarding the death of a *muhsan*. It highlights the gravity of false testimony leading to execution, where the witness's subsequent claim determines whether he pays blood money (*diya*) or faces capital punishment himself, reflecting the high evidentiary standards for *hudud* crimes.
